Figure caption: Determining the cellular uptake of the nanoparticles in (A) 2D (scale bar represents 10 μM) and (B) 3D cultures (scale bar represents 100 μM): Uptake of nanoparticles in U87 cells and evaluation of internalization rates in 3D spheroid GBM cultures were studied using coumarin-6 loaded nanoparticles. Post-treatment, yellow puncta observed in U87 cells confirmed nanoparticle internalization, aligning with the mitochondria. Additionally, increased green fluorescence in the spheroid cultures post-treatment further validated the internalization of the formulations. Statistical comparisons between two groups were performed using unpaired t tests, while one-way and two-way ANOVA were applied for multiple group comparisons under identical or varying experimental conditions. Analyses were conducted using GraphPad Prism 8. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Significance levels are indicated as follows: *p ≤ 0.03, **p ≤ 0.002, and ***p < 0.00019.

Figure caption: Investigation of the internalization pathway of coumarin-6-loaded nanoparticles in U87 cells using endocytosis inhibitors: The internalization route of nanoparticles in U87 cells was investigated using various endocytosis inhibitors. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that the nanoparticles primarily utilize caveolae-mediated and dynamin-mediated endocytosis, while inhibiting macropinocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis showed no impact on nanoparticle uptake. Here, the following abbreviations were used: D = dynasore; G = genistein; C = chlorpromazine; N = nocodazole. Significance levels are indicated as follows: *p ≤ 0.03, **p ≤ 0.002, and ***p < 0.00019.

Figure caption: Evaluation of the cytotoxic effects of drug-loaded nanoparticles compared to free drugs in U87 cells after 48 h of treatment: (A) To evaluate the cytotoxic effects of the nanoformulations, an MTT assay was conducted at varying doses and compared with free drugs. The results showed that Dox-loaded SLNs had an IC50 value of approximately 450 μM, while Gem-loaded SLNs demonstrated a lower IC50 value of around 200 μM, indicating superior efficiency compared to the free drugs (IC50 value of free DOX is around 750 μM and that of Gem is around 300 μM) and (B) annexin V–PI assay confirmed the total number of dead cells post-treatment in both U87 and LN229 cell lines, validating the MTT results. Significance levels are indicated as follows: *p ≤ 0.03, **p ≤ 0.002, and ***p < 0.00019.

Figure caption: (A) Assessment of cytotoxic effects of formulations on 3D spheroid cultures using PI staining and measurement of spheroid size reduction post-treatment via phase contrast imaging: The impact of the nanoformulations was assessed in 3D spheroid cultures of Glioblastoma cells. An increase in red fluorescence intensity over time post-treatment indicated a time-dependent rise in the toxic effects of the nanoparticles on GBM cells (scale bar represents 100 μM). (B) Additionally, phase contrast imaging revealed a reduction in spheroid size following treatment, further demonstrating the formulations’ effectiveness in targeting the cells. Scale bar represents 20 μM. Significance levels are indicated as follows: *p ≤ 0.03, **p ≤ 0.002, and ***p < 0.00019.

Figure caption: Quantification of protein levels of PCNA and cleaved caspase-3 post-treatment in the U87 cells, along with p62 and LC3b levels, to assess autophagic pathway inhibition: Western blot analysis revealed a significant reduction in the expression of the proliferation marker PCNA in GBM cells treated with (A) DOX-loaded and (B) GEM-loaded SLNs, as well as free drugs, compared to untreated cells. Enhanced levels of the apoptotic marker, cleaved caspase-3, further confirmed the efficacy of the formulations, and (C) similar results were observed in 3D spheroid cultures of U87 cells. Additionally, increased expression of autophagy markers p62 and LC3B indicated the inhibition of autophagic flux post-treatment, leading to heightened cellular stress, disrupted homeostasis, and increased cell death in Glioblastoma cells. A p value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Significance levels are indicated as follows: *p ≤ 0.03, **p ≤ 0.002, and ***p < 0.00019.
